column1: # AUTHORED. The plant species in the CDS database, and why each one is in.
# Hosts are in the database as a SINK: without them a plant read is absorbed by the nearest
# fungal CDS and reported as a fungal hit (02_build/README.md). They are NOT there to be
# db_v3 held 38 plant species / 568 M minimizers / 11.8% of the database, from an era when the
# cohort spanned 36 hosts. The literature-first cohort is four cereals, so 32 species are
# dropped: 413 M minimizers, 8.6% of db_v3. See exclusions.tsv.
# WHY NOT JUST THE FOUR: 04_assign/host RANKS reads across hosts rather than thresholding, so
# with only cohort hosts in the database every library is called as one of them and a
# mislabelled or contaminated non-cereal library becomes undetectable. That ranking is how
# Fragaria's absence was found (30 strawberry runs landing on Populus, Arachis and Glycine) and
# what the 228 low_coverage calls flag. Two outgroups keep that signal for ~20 M minimizers.

column5: cohort crop; 1,120 runs, never yet classified

dropped from the cohort under the 100-run figure floor but still a cereal with real detections, and the nearest monocot outgroup. Note the barley in the kraken charts is mostly wheat (host calls are one-directionally biased in rust surveys), so it also serves as the control on that bias.
dicot outgroup for mislabel QC. Phylogenetically distant from the cereals, so a library that ranks here is almost certainly not a cereal.
